sentences.text: The MFA No.200316/2021 is preferred by the appellant/Corporation to whom the offending bus bearing Reg.No.KA-38/F-538 belonged and the MFA No.200968/2021 is preferred by the legal representatives of deceased Mamata D/o Ramesh Sagar challenging the judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Aurad-B (for short, 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.114/2018 dated 01.10.2020.

The appeal preferred by the claimants is on the ground of inadequate and meager compensation whereas, the appeal preferred by the Corporation is to set-aside the impugned judgment and award as being erroneous, illegal and perverse.
2. The parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Briefly stated, the facts are that, petitioners are the parents of deceased Mamata who suffered severe injuries in a road accident that took place on 15.10.2017 at 9.15 a.m., at the Bridge near Shalyal village on Aurad-Tondchi- Udgir road within the limits of Udgir Rural Police Station, by toppling down of bus bearing registration No.KA-38/F-538 and later she succumbed to the injuries.
Petitioners claimed compensation of `47,00,000/-.

They pleaded that deceased was aged 21 years,
working as Nurse in Indumathi Hospital at Udgir and earning `20,000/- per month.
4.
The claim was opposed by the Corporation.
The Tribunal awarded `9,79,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

5. The petitioners have pleaded inadequacy in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, income taken on lower side, future prospects was not added, less amounts have been awarded towards conventional heads.
6.
It is the further case of the petitioners that the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged 21 years at the time of her death.
She was working as Nurse and was earning `20,000/- per annum with bonus and allowances.
From the said income, she used to contribute the entire salary for the maintenance of the petitioners family.
It is stated that because of her untimely death, the petitioners have lost their earning member.
Petitioners being the father and mother of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their daughter and have been put to great mental shock.
The petitioners were depending upon deceased's income.
Therefore, it is claimed by the petitioners to award compensation of `47,00,000/- under all the heads.
7. Before the learned Tribunal, pursuant to the notice, respondents appeared and resisted the petition by filing detailed objections.
However, they admitted the occurrence of accident.
The allegations of rash and negligent driving of the said bus by the driver and the earning capacity of the deceased have been flatly denied by the respondents.
The claim of the petitioners as per the say of the respondents is exorbitant.
Hence, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. Based upon the rival pleadings, the learned Tribunal framed the following issues:
1.

Whether petitioners prove that on 15.10.2017 at 9.15 a.m. at the Bridge near Shalyal Village on Aurad-Tondchi- The Divisional Controller vs Shobha And Anr on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113076339/
3 Udgir road within the limits of Udgir Rural P.S the driver of vehicle No.KA-38/F-538 drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and personal safety of others and while driving so, he toppled down his vehicle and thereby caused the accident ?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Mamata D/o Ramesh as inmate of the vehicle No.KA-38/F-538 sustained fatal injuries in the accident and died on the spot?
3. Whether the petitioners prove age and income of the deceased ?
4. Whether the respondent proves that the petitioner No.2 is not entitled for compensation and that the potion by him is not maintainable ?
5. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, under what head/s, from whom and in what quantum ?
6. What order or award?
9. Before the Tribunal, on behalf of petitioners, petitioners entered the witness box, examined as PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Ex.P1 to P9 and closed petitioners evidence.

On the other hand,
respondent/Corporation neither examined any witness nor produced any documents on its behalf.

10. The learned Tribunal, having heard the arguments, allowed the petition in-part by awarding compensation of `9,79,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till payment.

11. It is this judgment and award which is challenged by the appellants who are petitioners before the Tribunal being dissatisfied with the compensation so awarded and according to them, the compensation so awarded is inadequate and is opposed to the probabilities of the case.
There is no proper awarding of compensation towards conventional heads.
The income of the deceased was not properly assessed and taken by the Tribunal.
In fact, the monthly income of the deceased was to be enhanced to `10,250/-.
Therefore, it is prayed that the appeal be allowed and compensation be enhanced.
Respondent/Corporation is before this Court seeking to set aside the judgment and award.
12. We have heard the arguments of both sides at length and perused the record.
13. The learned Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at `6,000/- per month and deducted 1/3rd towards her personal expenses.

After deduction, the income was calculated at `4,000/-
(6000-1/3rd) per month.
Towards other conventional heads, the compensation is awarded.
As per judgment rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (Smt.) & Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 case, the multiplier applied was `18'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus,
the Tribunal has awarded `8,64,000/- (4000x12x18) towards loss of dependency and `1,15,000/-
under conventional heads.
Totally an amount of `9,79,000/- was awarded to the petitioners.

4 14.

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Shobha And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued by the counsel for the appellants- petitioners that the compensation so awarded is inadequate as the Tribunal has taken monthly income of the deceased at `6,000/- which is on the lower side.
As per the notional income chart prescribed by the Legal Services Authority to the accident of the year 2017, the income has to be taken at `10,250/- per month.

Therefore, he submits that, notional income has to be taken into consideration depending upon the year of accident and other aspects as per the law laid down in the Judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.
15.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is relevant to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Syed Basheer Ahmed vs. Mohammed Zameer reported in (2009) 2 SCC 225 wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court noticed that Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act enjoins the claims Tribunal to make an award determining "the amount of compensation which appears to be just".

entities.text: Syed Basheer Ahmed vs. Mohammed Zameer reported in (2009) 2 SCC 225
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, the objective factors,
which may constitute the basis of compensation appearing as just, have not been indicated in the Act.
Thus, the expression "which appears to be just" vests wide discretion in the Claims Tribunal in the matter of determination of compensation.

Nevertheless, the wide amplitude of such power does not empower the Tribunal to determine the compensation arbitrarily or to ignore settled principles relating to the determination of the compensation.

Similarly, although the Act is a beneficial legislation, it can neither be allowed to be used as a source of profit nor as a windfall to the persons affected nor should it be punitive to the persons liable to pay compensation.

The determination of the compensation must be based on certain data, establishing reasonable nexus between the loss incurred by the dependents of the deceased and the compensation to be awarded to them.
In a nutshell, the amount of compensation determined to be payable to the claimants has to be fair and reasonable by accepted legal standards.

16. The determination of the quantum must answer what "contemporary society would deem to be a fair sum such as would allow the wrong doer to hold up his head among his neighbours and say with their approval that he has done the fair thing".
The amount awarded must not be niggardly since the "law values life and limb in a free Society in generous case".

At the same time, misplaced sympathy,
generosity and benevolence cannot be the guiding factor for determining compensation.

The object of providing compensation is to please the petitioners to the extent possible, in almost the same financial position as they were in before the accident and not to make a fortune out of misfortune that has befallen them.

17. Keeping in mind the aforesaid analogy with regard to awarding of just compensation, as in this case the inadequacy of compensation is challenged by the petitioners- appellants, we restrict our findings only with regard to inadequacy of the compensation.
18. Evidently, the deceased Mamata was working as Nurse in Indumathi Hospital at Udgir.

If the notional income of the deceased is taken at `10,250/- and as per the judgment in Pranay Sethi stated supra, there would be an addition of 40% (40% of `10,250 is `4,100/-) to the said income, if calculated, the income of the deceased would be `14,350/-.
As the deceased was spinster, 50% of her income is to be deducted towards her personal expenses.
The annual income would be `86,100/- (7175x12).

The deceased was aged 22 years at the time of accident and as per the decision in the case of Sarala Varma and others vs. Delhi Transport The Divisional Controller vs Shobha And Anr on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113076339/
5 Corporation and another (2009 ACJ 1298), the proper multiplier applicable is `18'.

entities.text: Sarala Varma and others vs. Delhi Transport The Divisional Controller vs Shobha And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the total loss of dependency would be `15,49,800/- (7175x12x18).
19.
Petitioners are the parents of the deceased have lost their beloved daughter being bread earner.
Towards loss of consortium, certain amount is to be awarded to the petitioners.
Petitioners have lost their daughter and also lost her love and affection towards them.
Therefore, towards filial love and affection, petitioners are entitled to some compensation.
So also, because of untimely death of deceased Mamata, there is loss of estate.
So also, the petitioners must have spent substantial amount towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
Therefore, certain amount is to be awarded towards funeral expenses and obsequies ceremonies.
20. As already MACT has awarded compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a which is challenged in this case, the same interest is to be awarded on the amount so enhanced in this appeal.

Thus the petitioners-appellants are entitled for compensation as under:
 Sl.No. Heads `
 1. Loss of dependency 15,49,800/-
 (7,175*12*18)
 2. Towards loss of consortium 80,000/-
 3. Funeral and obsequies 15,000/-
 ceremonies

4 . Loss of Estate 15,000/-
 TOTAL 16,59,800/-
 Less : Comp. awarded by the Tribunal 9,79,000/-

Amount of compensation enhanced in 6,80,800/-
 appeal  Rounded off to 6,81,000/-
21.
In view of our discussion, with regard to the actionable claim and the compensation to be awarded to the claimants, the appeal filed by the claimants deserves to be allowed in-part.

Resultantly, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal filed by appellant-Corporation in MFA No.200316/2021 is dismissed and the appeal filed by the petitioners in MFA No.200968/2021 is allowed in-part.
ii) The Judgment and Award dated 01.10.2020 passed in MVC No.114/2018 by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and MACT, Aurad-B is modified.
